name: Navbar
description: The navigation bar at the top of a site or app: the logo, links to the main sections, and optional actions such as search. It marks the current page and wraps onto more rows on small screens.
whenToUse: Once per page, at the top, for the site’s or app’s main sections.
With up to about five top-level destinations.

whenNotToUse.text: To switch views within one page.
For secondary links such as Privacy.

anatomy.name: Bar
anatomy.description: The navigation landmark; surface follows the section tokens.

anatomy.name: Items
anatomy.description: Links to the main sections; the current one is highlighted and underlined.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: Search, buttons or an avatar at the end.

values.meaning: A link to another page. Use for navigation.
A button that runs onClick, for app views without URLs.

states.name: Current
states.meaning: Tinted, brand-colored and underlined; announced as “current page”.

behavior.text: Set currentItem from your router. Uncontrolled, clicking an item makes it current.
Items and actions wrap onto more rows instead of scrolling or hiding.
The Navbar doesn’t position itself; make it sticky or absolute in page CSS.
Give each navigation landmark a different aria-label (default “Main”).

content: Use short, familiar labels: one or two words (“Products”, “Pricing”).
Order items by importance or by the user’s journey.

guidelines.do: Mark the current page with currentItem.
guidelines.dont: Style the current item with a custom class.
guidelines.why: aria-current tells screen reader users where they are; a class only changes the look.

guidelines.dont: Use onClick-only buttons for navigation between URLs.
guidelines.why: Links can be opened in a new tab, bookmarked and shared.

guidelines.do: Keep it to about five items.
guidelines.dont: Squeeze every page into the top bar.
guidelines.why: Too many items wrap into a crowded bar and are hard to scan.

accessibility.role: navigation landmark (nav) with a list of links.

keyboard.action: Moves through the logo, items and actions in order.
Follows a link or activates a button item.

aria.when: Always: the label names the item.

accessibility.focus: Each item shows the focus ring.

wcag.how: A nav landmark containing a list.
The current item is also underlined (and underlined text in forced colors).
Items wrap at narrow widths without horizontal scrolling.

examples.title: Site navigation
examples.description: Logo, links and the current page.

examples.title: With actions
examples.description: A sign-in button at the end.

examples.title: With a router
examples.description: Drive the current item from the URL.

related.relation: For switching views within a page.

changes: Real links (or buttons) in a labelled nav list, replacing clickable divs; aria-current marks the current page.
currentItem / defaultCurrentItem / onCurrentItemChange replace defaultActiveItem; items take href and a ReactNode icon; new actions slot.
Own --navbar-* tokens instead of --menu-item-*; no fixed width or absolute positioning.

components.name: Navbar
components.description:
The site's main navigation bar: logo, links to the top-level pages, and optional
actions. The current page is marked with aria-current.

items.description: The main destinations; keep to about five.

currentItem.description: Id of the current page's item (controlled).

defaultCurrentItem.description: Initially current item when uncontrolled; clicking an item makes it current.

onCurrentItemChange.description: Called with the item id when an item is clicked.

actions.description: Content at the end of the bar, e.g. a Button or an Avatar.

--navbar-item-active-icon-color.description: Main tone-colored text on light or tinted backgrounds: titles, active items.
